newsitem.title: USA: New test flight for TWA crash investigators.
newsitem.headline: New test flight for TWA crash investigators.

text.p: In the latest effort to solve the mystery of the TWA Flight 800 disaster, investigators will board an aircraft on Monday for a test flight retracing the path of the doomed plane, officials said.

The test flight from New York's John F. Kennedy international airport is one of several experiments investigators expect to make this week, the first anniversary of the tragic crash that killed all 230 people on board.
Investigators know an explosion in the Boeing 747's center fuel tank caused the disintegration of the plane off Long Island on July 17 last year, but they have not determined why.

The plane broke up in mid-air without warning just minutes after taking off from New York on a journey to Paris. FBI officials say there is no evidence a criminal act such as a bomb or a missile destroyed the plane, but they are not ready to declare that a catastrophic mechanical fault caused the crash.

National Transportation Safety Board Chairman Jim Hall said in a television interview on Sunday that the Boeing 747 used for the test flight would be loaded with more than 150 sensors to monitor temperatures in the fuel tank as the plane reaches the altitude at which the explosion occurred.
Investigators also will try to understand how possible movement of the tank might have affected the build-up of vapors, he said.
Officials said there were potential dangers for the nine to 11 experts who will take the test flight, but they would take precautions.
"The whole center tank will be very highly instrumented," Hall said in an interview on CNN.

The test flight will help investigators determine how explosive the mix of fuel and air fumes were in the nearly empty center fuel tank and how much energy might have been needed to trigger the explosion.
